title: What that general will is said to do: give the Son for all and offer converting grace to all
pass_a_gloss: According to which will namely, 1. He gave His only-begotten Son, who by His death would merit for all & each righteousness & life, by universal Redemption. 2. He also offers His Grace to all & each, no one excluded, through universal Vocation; ready to confer that Grace on all through ordinary means, or to call all through the Word of the Gospel, to convert all, regenerate, justify, adopt, & glorify, provided that human beings themselves do not place an obstacle? Affirm. Lutheran. Neg. Orthodox.
pass_b_english: Under that will, then, two claims are put: first, that He gave His only-begotten Son so that by His death the Son would merit righteousness and life for every person, through a universal Redemption; second, that He also offers His grace to every person, excluding none, through a universal vocation, and stands ready to confer that grace on all by the ordinary means — calling all through the Word of the Gospel, and converting, regenerating, justifying, adopting, and glorifying all — if only human beings do not place an obstacle in the way.
Lutherans affirm this; the Orthodox deny it.
source_text: Secundum quam nempè voluntatem, 1. Filium suum unigenitum dedit, qui promereretur suâ morte omnibus & singulis justitiam & vitam, universali Redemptione. 2. Offert etiam Gratiam suam omnibus & singulis, nemine excluso, per Vocationem universalem; paratus conferre omnibus eam Gratiam per ordinaria media, seu omnes vocare per Verbum Evangelii, omnes convertere, regenerare, justificare, adoptare, & glorificare, modò homines ipsi non obicem ponant? Affirm. Luth. Neg. Orth.

choices.why: Orth. = Reformed Orthodox side in Strimesius's usage here
